source.author: ov
source.text: Iamque erat in totas sparsurus fulmina terras: sed timuit, ne forte sacer tot ab ignibus aether conciperet flammas longusque ardesceret axis: esse quoque in fatis reminiscitur, affore tempus, quo mare, quo tellus correptaque regia caeli ardeat et mundi moles obsessa laboret.
source.text_original: Iamque erat in totas sparsurus fulmina terras: / sed timuit, ne forte sacer tot ab ignibus aether / conciperet flammas longusque ardesceret axis: / esse quoque in fatis reminiscitur, affore tempus, / quo mare, quo tellus correptaque regia caeli / ardeat et mundi moles obsessa laboret.
source.text_english: And now he was about to hurl lightning over the whole earth; but he feared lest the sacred air might by chance catch fire from so many flames and the long axle of heaven burn up. He also remembers that it is in the fates that the time will come when the sea, when the earth, and heaven’s seized realm will burn, and the great mass of the world, besieged, will be in distress.

reuse.text_original: esse quoque in fatis reminiscitur affore tempus quo mare, quo tellus correptaque regia caeli ardeat et mundi moles operosa laboret.
reuse.text_english: He also remembers that it is fated that a time will come when the sea, when the earth, and the palace of heaven caught fire will burn, and the laboring mass of the world will be in turmoil.
